workers_limits.subrequest_definition: fetch plus calls to R2, KV and D1
workers_limits.cpu_note: waiting on network requests, KV reads or database queries does not count as CPU time
workers_limits.duration: no hard limit for HTTP-triggered Workers

official_docs.drift_vs_previous_verification: NONE (limit tables identical to the 2026-10-03 copy)
official_docs.wrangler_toml_overrides: none: no [limits] section, so the default 30 s CPU and the default subrequest limit apply

evaluation.D1_HARD_LIMIT_COMPATIBILITY: PASS: operational ceiling 800 < 1000; largest measured invocation 763; 20% margin
evaluation.SUBREQUEST_COMPATIBILITY: PASS: runtime needs at most 801 per invocation (800 counted D1 statements + 1 source request, counting every statement individually) <= 10000; runner is sequential
evaluation.CPU_LIMIT_COMPATIBILITY: PARTIAL: officially compatible (30 s default; D1/fetch waiting is not CPU time); live CPU is NOT yet proven, the first canary provides that evidence
evaluation.PAUSE_RESUME_COMPATIBILITY: PASS: every operator POST is a distinct Worker invocation with its own D1 counter; the 100-study run needs 11,258 statements over 14 invocations, each <= 763
evaluation.CURRENT_800_STATEMENT_BUDGET: SAFE on the owner-confirmed Paid plan

capacity_write.reason: the only approved write path is the OPS_TOKEN-authenticated operator control route; the OPS_TOKEN secret exists on the Worker but its value is not available to the agent. Direct SQL, secret rotation or reading the secret were deliberately not used.
